messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. I don’t know the will’s exact wording or the estate’s debts and other assets; we need to check the documents. I want a fair financial share. I’m not agreeing to A buying the house at a discount that comes out of my share. I’d consider a buyout or sale once the house is properly valued. There’s no real deadline, so I don’t want this rushed. My relationship with A matters, but it doesn’t make an unfair price okay.

I don’t know the will’s exact terms or whether it leaves the house equally; I’d need to check the will before saying. There’s no price or independent valuation yet, and I haven’t worked out financing or a timeline. I do want to buy with my husband at a family discount, but C hasn’t agreed, so nothing is settled. I’d want B and C treated fairly for their shares; I’m not sure yet how that should be worked out. I agree B should speak for herself, and a valuation before discussing a discount seems fair.

Thank you. I don’t have a copy of the will, so I’m not sure what it says about the house or how it’s divided. I would like money to start a dance studio, but I haven’t worked out an amount or timing yet. I’d be open to being bought out, though I don’t know the right arrangement. A buying the house might be possible, but I’d want a valuation first and to understand what each of us would receive; I don’t think the discount is settled. I’d like to be included before anything is decided.
The list is fair. I don’t know who has the will or who the executor is. I’m okay with a loose target date to get the will and valuation, as long as it doesn’t force a decision or a discounted sale.

I don’t know who has the will or who’s executor. Yes, I’ll hold off on a price offer until the will and valuation are available. I don’t have a discount amount in mind yet or know where it would come from; I wouldn’t want it taken from my sisters’ shares without their agreement.

I don’t know who has the will or who is executor, so finding the will sounds like the right first step. I don’t disagree with the list; using the person’s own share for any discount seems fair to me. I can try to work out a rough amount and date for the studio, but I can’t give you one yet.

I can check Dad’s papers at home. Two weeks is a reasonable target for gathering information, not a deadline for a decision. And item 5 isn’t settled for me: A’s offer to fund a discount from her share doesn’t mean I’ve agreed to a discounted purchase.
I can contact the solicitor and look into whether there’s a will register. Two weeks is a reasonable target to make those enquiries, though I can’t promise the will will be found by then.
I can contact the bank and aim for the two-week target, though I can’t promise they have the will or will respond in time.

In principle, yes, if the independent valuation and my share are clear. I’m not committing before we know what the will says and what the estate owes. If A won’t pay the full valued price, I’d prefer considering a sale.
I’m not sure we could buy at the full valued price. I’d still prefer to buy at a family discount, if B and C agree. If they don’t, selling the house may be the realistic option.

In principle, I’d be open to A buying it at the full independently valued price, rather than selling, as long as my share of the proceeds is clear. I can’t say more until we know the will, the estate’s debts, and the value.

Yes, that’s closer to what I mean: I’d use my share toward the house’s value and pay B and C for theirs, not ask them to accept less. I don’t yet know whether we could raise two thirds of the valuation.
Thank you. The studio matters to me, but I don’t want to rush into accepting less than my share is worth. I’ll wait for the will and valuation before deciding.
Thanks for the summary. I agree that no option is chosen until we’ve read the will and had an independent valuation. I haven’t agreed to a discount; any proposal still needs to protect my fair share.
